authority: docs/system-design.html is the canonical L1-L9 architecture; this file maps the tree onto it. Task 044 asserts THIS mapping, not set equality, which is why the 11 targets -> 9 published layers relation is written out rather than inferred.

nonLayerPeers.install: Declared non-layer peer. It installs and packages the engine rather than sitting in its call graph, so it is a sibling of L1-L9, not a tenth layer.

splitNote: L5 (Dispatch core) is the one layer served by two target directories: `contract` (what may be called, and its authority) and `dispatch` (the single function that calls it). They are split because the contract is asserted independently of the dispatcher that honours it.

adapters.reason: CLI and MCP over one dispatch core — L8 itself.

architecture.reason: Conformance scanners and seam audits. They read the tree; they are not part of it. Extraction named in the plan.

cli.reason: Follow-loop and formatter are CLI adapter surface.

config.reason: Cross-cutting by nature, but its output is the resolved config the dispatch context and workflow guards read. Placed at its consumer, not split.

contract.reason: Authority collection, digests, IR and admission — the contract half of the L5 split. Task 014 folded schemas/, sdk/ and shared/ in: all three are contract surface.

describe.reason: L7 names describe explicitly among its generic windows over the log.

dispatch.reason: Caller identity, dispatch context, elicitation dispatch — the dispatch half of the L5 split. Task 014 folded core/ in: context.ts and dispatch.ts ARE the single dispatch function L5 describes.

events.reason: Append, expected-sequence, idempotency, the composite reader — L2 itself. Task 012 renamed event-store/ to match its target.

hooks.reason: Hook config is an adapter-side integration point.

install.reason: Atomic promotion and freshness checks. Declared NON-layer peer: it installs the engine rather than sitting in its call graph.

lifecycle.reason: Command bodies invoked by the CLI adapter; the logic is verb-shaped, the surface is not. Task 017 moved it from `cli-commands/` to its L7 target.

mcp.reason: MCP wire methods (elicitation, notifications, tasks) are adapter surface.

ndjson.reason: Frame encoding and heartbeat are transport framing beneath the adapters.

projections.reason: Pure reducers, cursors, snapshot/rebuild — L3 itself. Task 012 folded views/, telemetry/, quality/, session/ and task-store/ in as subdirectories; each remains a read model that derives and never decides.

pruner.reason: Prune coordinator and scoring are a composite-tool action.

registry.reason: The tool-declaration authority, decomposed out of one 4,587-line module. Classified with the contract half of L5 because the contract compiler derives its meta-model from these declarations. It keeps its own directory at the root of src/ rather than nesting under contract/: every layer's schemas feed INTO the declarations, so nesting would point the contract layer's import surface at the whole tree.

review.reason: Review dispatch, classifier and check catalog are composite-tool actions.

runbooks.reason: Resolved here per plan: runbooks are generic operator windows, the same shape as ps/describe/wait/export.

runtime.reason: Environment detection and command shims — L9 itself.

storage.reason: The SQLite backend, its lifecycle and the sidecar merger — L1 itself. Task 012 folded artifacts/ in: the content-addressed store is persistence, and its path-containment guards travel with it.

sync.reason: Outbox and sync handler are lifecycle-shaped generic windows, not workflow primitives.

utils.reason: atomic-write, paths, process, task-id: genuinely cross-cutting with consumers in five layers. Splitting it is a task 020 decision, not a naming one; recorded unresolved rather than forced.

vcs.reason: GitHub/GitLab/ADO providers adapt an external system; same shape as L8.

verbs.reason: The action bodies behind the composite tools — the largest single directory in the tree (159 files) and squarely L6. Task 015 regrouped it from a flat `orchestrate/` into capability families; it now sits at its target.

workflow.reason: State machines, phase contracts, guards, checkpoint — L4 itself. Task 013 folded topology/ in: the phase-contract loader and staleness signal are workflow-primitive data, not a layer of their own.

staleEntriesNote: Task 043 removed src/__tests__ and src/commands and their entries here. Both were disposition:exception "(stays test-adjacent)" describing 44 and 3 test files that task 030 had already lifted into tests/ — so the directories had been EMPTY since then, tracked by nothing, and invisible to every census that reads git rather than the filesystem. The exceptions are discharged, not violated: their contents went exactly where the entries said they belonged. Counts re-derived from the live tree, 28 -> 26 directories.
